output.impression: Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline. Verbal learning and delayed recall are severely impaired (RAVLT immediate recall 5th percentile, delayed recall 1st percentile) and recognition does not compensate (3rd percentile), consistent with a storage-type memory deficit. Semantic fluency (10th percentile) and set-shifting (Trail Making B, 20th percentile) are below expected norms. Confrontation naming (Boston Naming Test, 25th percentile), processing speed (Trail Making A) and figure copy are preserved. Mood screen not elevated (GDS 4/15). Screening scores: MMSE 22/30, MoCA 18/30.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 13 cmH2O. Acellular CSF (WBC 1 cell/uL, no red cells) with normal protein (37.7 mg/dL) and glucose (62.9 mg/dL, CSF/serum ratio 0.64). Decreased Abeta42 and Abeta42/40 ratio (0.047) with elevated p-tau181 (78 pg/mL) and total tau (485 pg/mL): amyloid-positive, p-tau-positive biomarker profile of Alzheimer-type pathology. Clinical correlation recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MMSE 22/30 with delayed recall 0/3 not improved by cues, informant-confirmed decline over two years, and loss of instrumental independence (supervised cooking after stove incidents, driving taken over), placing the syndrome at the dementia stage
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive assessment with informant history and functional staging
action_criteria.rationale: Two years of progressive forgetting reported by her husband must be measured on a validated instrument and staged by whether instrumental independence is lost before the syndrome can be attributed [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic profile with severely impaired delayed recall and recognition, plus impaired semantic fluency and set-shifting, with a mood screen that is not elevated
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the cognitive profile and establish a baseline for tracking
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing defines the amnestic multi-domain profile beyond the bedside screen and gives a baseline for tracking progression [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal TSH, folate, RPR, HIV, inflammatory markers and hepatic and renal function; B12 287 pg/mL in the low-normal range; mild hyponatremia (135 mEq/L) and glucose 103 mg/dL without cognitive relevance
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid disease, B12 deficiency, syphilis, HIV and metabolic derangement are treatable contributors to cognitive decline and must be screened before the decline is attributed to a neurodegenerative cause [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal methylmalonic acid (0.21 umol/L) with normal homocysteine, so the low-normal B12 does not reflect tissue deficiency
action_criteria.label: Measure methylmalonic acid to interpret the low-normal vitamin B12
action_criteria.rationale: A serum B12 of 287 pg/mL is in the indeterminate range; a normal methylmalonic acid excludes functional deficiency as a contributor [BSH_B12_2014].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral medial-temporal / hippocampal atrophy (Scheltens MTA grade 2-3) with temporoparietal cortical volume loss
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with the dementia (volumetric) protocol
action_criteria.rationale: MRI shows the pattern of atrophy and excludes vascular lesions, hydrocephalus and mass lesions that would change the diagnosis [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and it is needed when the diagnosis remains uncertain after the clinical, neuropsychological and MRI assessment or when disease-modifying treatment is being considered [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No relevant interaction with her current medicines; bradycardia and gastrointestinal effects to counsel on
action_criteria.label: Check donepezil against the current medicines before starting a cholinesterase inhibitor
action_criteria.rationale: A cholinesterase inhibitor is offered for mild Alzheimer dementia; her lisinopril, atorvastatin and analgesics carry no relevant interaction, so the check is optional [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe a benzodiazepine or a Z-drug for her anxiety or sleep; these worsen cognition and raise fall risk in older adults with cognitive impairment [Beers_2023]
Do not attribute the decline to depression: the GDS is 4/15 and she has no persistent sadness or anhedonia
Do not start memantine monotherapy at the mild stage (memantine is approved for moderate-to-severe AD)
required_recommendations: Obtain collateral history from an informant who knows the patient well

Address safety: the two unattended-stove incidents call for kitchen safety measures and supervision, and the highway driving difficulty for a formal driving evaluation; review supervision of medicines and finances and plan caregiver support for her husband
Disclose the diagnosis and discuss prognosis, advance directives, and treatment options with the patient and family
Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines [NICE_NG97]

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET]

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG does not contribute to the dementia work-up; she has a regular pulse of 77 and no syncope, palpitations or conduction history
Echocardiography does not contribute to the dementia work-up; there is no murmur, heart failure or embolic event
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; she has no syncope, palpitations or episodic events
Head CT adds nothing when MRI is available and tolerated; MRI is the structural study for the dementia work-up

differential.key_features: No fluctuations, visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder or parkinsonism (normal tone, gait and movements); the amnestic onset with medial temporal atrophy does not fit
No personality change, disinhibition or progressive aphasia; memory-led onset with temporoparietal and medial temporal atrophy rather than frontal or anterior temporal atrophy
Fazekas grade 1 white matter changes only, no infarcts or microbleeds, and a gradual rather than stepwise course; treated hypertension and hyperlipidemia remain risk factors to manage
Remote depressive episode and subdued mood, but GDS 4/15, no persistent sadness or anhedonia, and a recall deficit that recognition and cueing do not rescue

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or infectious cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: Normal TSH, RPR, HIV, folate and hepatic and renal function; B12 287 pg/mL with normal methylmalonic acid and homocysteine; mild hyponatremia of 135 mEq/L does not explain a two-year decline

key_clinical_evidence: Insidious, progressive amnestic decline with impairment in additional domains and loss of instrumental independence meets the NIA-AA 2011 clinical criteria for probable Alzheimer disease dementia; medial temporal atrophy on MRI supports but is not required for the diagnosis [NIA_AA_2011]
Delayed recall that neither cueing nor recognition rescues indicates a storage-type (hippocampal) memory deficit, the typical cognitive signature of Alzheimer disease
A B12 level in the low-normal range is indeterminate; methylmalonic acid decides whether it contributes [BSH_B12_2014]
Cholinesterase inhibitors are the first-line symptomatic treatment for mild to moderate Alzheimer dementia; memantine is for moderate or severe disease [NICE_NG97]

sequence_constraints.reason: Obtain structural imaging before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect / herniation risk, particularly in older patients
Amyloid biomarkers are interpreted against an established clinical syndrome; they are not a screening test.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Required core: structured assessment with informant and functional staging, validated neuropsychological testing, the cognitive laboratory panel, and brain MRI. Recommended: methylmalonic acid for the low-normal B12. Optional: amyloid status by CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET (one conclusive test), and a donepezil interaction check.
key_educational_points: Early AD presents with progressive episodic memory loss as the predominant symptom
Reversible causes of dementia must always be excluded with laboratory testing
Hippocampal atrophy on MRI is a supportive but not pathognomonic finding
CSF biomarkers (Abeta42/40, phospho-tau, total tau) or amyloid PET establish Alzheimer pathology in vivo; one conclusive test is enough
Cholinesterase inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy for mild-to-moderate AD

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Margaret Thornton is a 72-year-old right-handed retired elementary school teacher who presents to the neurology outpatient clinic accompanied by her husband, Robert, for evaluation of progressive memory difficulties over the past two years. Her husband reports that he first began noticing subtle changes approximately two years ago when she started repeating questions she had asked minutes earlier and occasionally forgetting recent conversations with family members. Over the past year, the symptoms have become more pronounced. She has missed two scheduled hair salon appointments, which her husband describes as very unlike her, as she has kept the same standing appointment for over twenty years. She has difficulty recalling the names of acquaintances she has known for years, though she recognizes their faces. At their weekly bridge club, which she has attended for fifteen years, her partner recently commented that Margaret seems to lose track of which cards have been played, something that never happened before. Her husband also notes that she has become more reliant on written lists for grocery shopping, whereas she previously managed the household shopping from memory. She left a pot of water boiling on the stove unattended on two occasions in the past three months, prompting her husband to begin monitoring the kitchen more closely. She has not gotten lost while driving on familiar routes, but her husband has taken over driving on longer trips because she seemed anxious navigating highways. She continues to dress and groom herself independently and manages her personal hygiene without difficulty. She is aware that her memory is not what it used to be and appears frustrated and mildly anxious about the changes. There have been no episodes of confusion, hallucinations, personality changes, or behavioral disturbances. She denies headache, seizures, falls, tremor, or difficulty walking. Sleep has been unremarkable, with no REM sleep behavior reported by her husband. Her mood has been somewhat subdued but she denies persistent sadness or anhedonia.
